claims.text: The coefficient ring is \(\Lambda=\Lambda(x_1,x_2,\ldots)\) with integral coefficients, \(I_{r,n-r}=\operatorname{Span}_{\mathbb Z}\{s_\lambda:\lambda\nsubseteq(n-r)^r\}\), and \(H^*(\mathrm{Gr}_{r,n})\cong\Lambda/I_{r,n-r}=:\overline\Lambda\). [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 89-94]

groundings.excerpt:
89: Let \Lambda=\Lambda(x_{1},x_{2},\ldots) be the ring of symmetric functions with integral coefficients. This space has a {\mathbb{Z}}-linear basis consisting of Schur functions s_{\lambda},
90: where \lambda is an integer partition. Consider the ideal
91: I_{r,n-r}=\mathrm{Span}_{\mathbb{Z}}\left\{s_{\lambda}\mid\lambda\nsubseteq(n-r)^{r}\right\}
92: of \Lambda. Then one has the following standard presentation of the cohomology of Grassmannians:
93: H^{*}(\mathrm{Gr}_{r,n})\cong\Lambda/I_{r,n-r}.
94: We will use an overline to denote the projection \Lambda\to\Lambda/I_{r,n-r}. Specifically, we will write \overline{\Lambda} as a shorthand for \Lambda/I_{r,n-r}. We will also distinguish between s_{\lambda}\in\Lambda, the usual Schur function, and \overline{s}_{\lambda} for its image in \overline{\Lambda}.

claims.text: Theorem 1.2 assumes a bigrassmannian \(v=v_{r,s,t,n}\in S_n\), defines \(i=s-t+1\), \(j=r-t+1\), \(a=\min(n-r-i,r-j)\), and \(b=\min(i,j)\), and concludes that \(J_v\), as an ideal of \(\overline\Lambda\), is minimally generated by \(\{\overline{s}_\mu:i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq(i^j,b^a)\}\); “minimality” means no generator can be removed. [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 95-110]
